ctc_tags.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_tags.rationale: Structured, reviewable workflows and approved source materials support inspectable tool use while remaining an external implementation signal, not learner evidence.
Iterative review and human approval provide a design analogy for keeping machine-generated intermediate states available for human reconsideration.

ctc_tags.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_tags.rationale: The solver and language model are treated as decision-support tools whose outputs are contextualized and sometimes overridden by humans rather than final authority.
Decision, rationale, expected outcome, actual outcome, and override are preserved as separate stages; this is mapped as a system-research analogy rather than student-learning evidence.
The practice world invites learners to try different strategies and decide how to improve their own approach within an explicit challenge.

ctc_tags.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_tags.rationale: Code Builder, AI-assisted approaches, and a timed world become manipulable computational media for strategy testing.
Repeated strategies and times can make changes in approach visible, although speed itself must not be mistaken for complete learning evidence.

ctc_tags.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_tags.rationale: The AI responds inside live performance as creative material rather than replacing the musician's interpretive role.
Real-time human-machine musical dialogue exemplifies reciprocal collaboration while remaining external research rather than TurtleBlock learner evidence.
Improvisation supplies a boundary case where too much explicit measuring or prompting could disrupt the activity being studied.
Criterion relations are attributed to interpreters instead of to the world, preserving the learner's role in deciding what an observation means for their inquiry.
A world event can counter an expectation and create a new problem without closing the inquiry with an automated verdict.

ctc_tags.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_tags.rationale: The world becomes an inspectable computational object-to-think-with whose facts can constrain thought without owning semantic meaning.
The contract preserves event, interpretation, relation, disagreement, and revision as distinguishable states that could later show learning-in-process.
Interpretations are separate from observations so people can compare what happened with what they thought it meant and revise accordingly.
The world may expose distributions, movement, access, or consequences but cannot label those facts fair, democratic, welcoming, or oppressive without an attributable interpreter.
The plural fixture demonstrates that collaborators can interpret the same world measurement differently without manufactured consensus.
The candidate was rejected because instrumentation itself can become surveillance or privilege measurable behavior before learner purpose and privacy boundaries are defined.
Automatic interpretation could replace learner-directed inquiry with machine-selected significance.
The next question asks whether learner purpose can govern what Turtle surfaces rather than letting machine salience become the curriculum.

ctc_tags.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_tags.rationale: Inspectable attention rules could make computational noticing manipulable rather than opaque.
The horizon asks when surfacing an event helps reflection and when restraint better preserves the learner's flow and agency.
Selecting what is measurable and noteworthy is a power-laden act that can privilege efficiency, compliance, visibility, or other values.
Different participants may legitimately want different attention filters around the same shared world.

ontology_tags.rationale: The envelope makes the reciprocal sequence from intention to world consequence to attributed interpretation and later revision inspectable without collapsing the participants.
Play can generate concrete surprises and measurements that become material for further inquiry without requiring a predetermined semantic verdict.
An inhabitable room of possibilities matters because represented ideas produce consequences people can encounter, interpret, and change.
The world event makes previously abstract assumptions visible as inspectable state while preserving the distinction between state and meaning.
Turtle's interpretation is represented as another attributable claim that can be examined rather than the authoritative account of the event.
One event may sustain competing interpretations, counterexamples, and new questions rather than forcing one normalized conclusion.
World observation, learner interpretation, collaborator interpretation, Turtle interpretation, and synthetic interpretation can coexist only when their origins and evidence classes remain distinct.
World consequence becomes pedagogically useful when it can return to reflection, revision, and another question rather than end as a verdict.
Event, interpretation, criterion relation, authority, privacy, and reversibility become explicit machine-checkable research structure.
The validator enforces evidence-class and actor distinctions that future retrieval must preserve rather than flatten.
The fixture tests the standing rule that synthetic Turtle material can never be reclassified as human interaction, although no actual self-play dialogue was run.
Surfacing an observation changes what participants attend to and therefore becomes part of the reciprocal system rather than a neutral transport act.
The edge explicitly asks when machine interruption would undermine the playful inquiry it intends to support.
A Turtle decision to surface or remain silent can itself become inspectable material rather than invisible authority.
Future attention records should preserve the event, selector, attention rule, surfacing decision, and later interpretation as distinct provenance states.

dissertation_code_mappings.rationale: Situated observation matters to the experiment, while the build explicitly refuses to equate observation with self-authenticating interpretation.
Meaning is constructed through interaction with experienced consequences rather than stored as an intrinsic property of the world event.
Unexpected world behavior can create a discoverable contradiction that changes subsequent inquiry.
A world observation may complicate a provisional answer and generate a better problem instead of closing the task.
Forbidding a world-authored semantic verdict prevents machine-readable outcomes from quietly becoming predetermined educational success criteria.
Learner judgment remains attributable, revisable, and distinct from Turtle or world claims.
The plural fixture preserves divergent participant interpretations rather than manufacturing consensus from one shared measurement.
What the system measures and surfaces can shape whose experiences and consequences become visible, making attention itself socially consequential.

emergent_tags.rationale: Names the central executable distinction introduced by the contribution.
Describes the representation pattern under test without promoting it into the formal ontology.
One observed fact may support different attributable readings.
Captures why the telemetry candidate was rejected before live instrumentation existed.
Names the unresolved question of who controls which observable events enter learner attention.
Preserves the possibility that non-interruption may sometimes be the most agency-protective Turtle action.
Easy-to-measure variables may become overrepresented in what the system treats as important.

uncaptured_observations.observation: Measurement is not interpretation, but measurement selection is not neutral by definition: choosing elapsed time, crowd count, entrances, or resource flow can already encode a human or system value before any later interpretation occurs.
uncaptured_observations.reason_unmapped: This may be best represented as instrumentation provenance and Social/Cultural Critique rather than as a new learner-development domain, but the recurring relationship between measurement selection and epistemic authority remains unsettled.

uncaptured_observations.observation: A computational world may materially constrain an interpretation without possessing human intention or interpretive agency; the phrase 'world as participant' is useful but theoretically incomplete.
uncaptured_observations.reason_unmapped: The existing evidence classes preserve origin, while the ontological status of non-intentional environmental influence inside co-active emergence remains unresolved.

uncaptured_observations.observation: Once observation is technically possible, selective noticing becomes a new power problem: deciding which of thousands of possible events deserve attention could become surveillance, unsolicited pedagogy, or rubricification even with perfect event provenance.
uncaptured_observations.reason_unmapped: This cuts across Personal Inquiry, Reflection, Social and Cultural Critique, privacy, and agency; it does not yet justify an eighth CTC domain.

uncaptured_observations.observation: Deliberate non-interruption can be meaningful agent behavior, yet recording every potential intervention Turtle chose not to make would create an impossible counterfactual audit and threaten capture-batch closure.
uncaptured_observations.reason_unmapped: Absence, restraint, and unrealized speech acts are not naturally represented by the current event-centric research object model.
